grammarPoint.title: Advanced relative clauses
grammarPoint.summary: Learn to use advanced relative clauses like 'whereby', 'in which', 'whose', 'of whom', and 'all of which' to add precise, detailed information to sentences.
grammarPoint.explanation:
Advanced relative clauses allow you to connect ideas more formally and precisely, often providing extra details about a noun. They help to create more sophisticated and concise sentences by combining two related statements into one.

*Whereby* introduces a method or process. *In which* can refer to a place or an abstract context. *Whose* indicates possession for both people and things, while *of whom* is a more formal way to show possession or a relationship, usually with people, especially when referring to a quantity from a group.

Phrases like *all of which*, *some of which*, or *many of whom* are used to refer to a part of a previously mentioned group of people or things. These clauses are typically non-defining, meaning they add extra, non-essential information and are usually separated by commas.

examples.text: The company implemented a new system, whereby employees can access their files remotely.
examples.note: Explains the method or process of the new system.

examples.text: The ancient manuscript, in which rare botanical illustrations were found, is now on display.
examples.note: Refers to the location or context where something was found.

examples.text: Dr. Anya Sharma, whose groundbreaking research was published last month, will give the keynote speech.
examples.note: Shows possession, indicating the research belongs to Dr. Sharma.

examples.text: The board interviewed ten candidates, three of whom were highly qualified for the position.
examples.note: Refers to a specific number from a group of people.

examples.text: She presented several innovative proposals, all of which received positive feedback from the committee.
examples.note: Refers to the entirety of a group of things mentioned previously.

commonErrors.wrong: The new policy, by which employees can work from home, is popular.
commonErrors.right: The new policy, whereby employees can work from home, is popular.
commonErrors.note: Use 'whereby' to introduce the method or means by which something happens.

commonErrors.wrong: The artist, who's paintings are very abstract, has a new exhibition.
commonErrors.right: The artist, whose paintings are very abstract, has a new exhibition.
commonErrors.note: 'Whose' shows possession; 'who's' is a contraction of 'who is' or 'who has'.

commonErrors.wrong: He has two brothers, both of them live abroad.
commonErrors.right: He has two brothers, both of whom live abroad.
commonErrors.note: Use 'of whom' (for people) or 'of which' (for things) after a quantity to refer back to the noun.

exercises.question: The university introduced a new scholarship program, ___ students from low-income backgrounds can receive full tuition.
exercises.explanation: 'Whereby' is used to introduce the method or means by which something is achieved.

exercises.question: The ancient city, ___ many historical artifacts were discovered, is a popular tourist destination.
exercises.explanation: 'In which' is used to refer to a place or context, often more formally than 'where'.

exercises.question: The author, ___ latest novel won a major award, will be signing books tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: 'Whose' is the possessive form of 'who' and is used to show that the novel belongs to the author.

exercises.question: The team presented five solutions to the problem, only two ___ were considered viable.
exercises.explanation: 'Of which' is used after a quantity to refer back to a group of things previously mentioned.

exercises.text: The new software includes a feature ___ users can customize their interface.
exercises.explanation: 'Whereby' introduces the method or means by which users can customize their interface.

exercises.text: The old factory, ___ my grandfather used to work, has been converted into apartments.
exercises.explanation: 'In which' refers to the location (the factory) where the action took place.

exercises.text: The research group consists of six scientists, four ___ are experts in climate modeling.
exercises.explanation: 'Of whom' is used after a quantity to refer to a specific number from a group of people.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
exercises.explanation: This sentence uses 'whose' to show that the lectures belong to the professor, adding extra information about him.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
exercises.explanation: This sentence uses 'all of which' to refer to the entire group of suggestions previously mentioned.

exercises.prompt: Find the mistake and write the sentence correctly.
exercises.sentence: The contract, by which both parties agreed to terms, was signed yesterday.
answers: The contract, whereby both parties agreed to terms, was signed yesterday.
The contract, under which both parties agreed to terms, was signed yesterday.
exercises.explanation: 'Whereby' is the correct word to introduce the method or means by which the agreement was reached.

exercises.prompt: Find the mistake and write the sentence correctly.
exercises.sentence: He introduced his colleagues, two of them I had met before.
answers: He introduced his colleagues, two of whom I had met before.
exercises.explanation: When referring to a quantity from a group of people, use 'of whom' to connect the clause.

exercises.source: The architect designed a building. Its innovative features won an award.
answers: The architect, whose innovative features won an award, designed a building.
exercises.explanation: 'Whose' connects the building to its features, showing possession and combining the ideas smoothly.

exercises.source: The report contained several key findings. All of them were surprising.
exercises.instruction: Rewrite the sentence using 'all of which'.
answers: The report contained several key findings, all of which were surprising.
exercises.explanation: 'All of which' refers back to the 'key findings' and introduces additional information about them.

many famous plays were performed, is now a museum.

pairs.left: The delegation included ten members, five of whom
pairs.right: were fluent in both English and French.
